_comment: Example site map for live Elasticsearch research (hider/elastic.py).
Every name here is invented. Copy this to a file outside the repository,
replace the index patterns and field names with your own, and point
HIDER_ELASTIC at it, or put the object under "elastic" in hider.local.json.
Index and field names describe the estate; they never belong in the repo.
Kinds: keep (declared non-sensitive, freely queryable; a stray value tier 1
recognises is still replaced, in hits and bucket keys), identifier (replaced by a
stable typed label; queried by label only), text (tiers 1+2 plus the sweep;
match_phrase only). A field that is not listed is dropped and unqueryable.
An identifier may carry a 'shape' regex with named groups and a 'label'
format using those groups plus {n}, so a server keeps its region:
ctr-amer-042 -> ctr-amer-s01. The label must not itself match the shape.
clusters maps a short name (what Claude sees) to a Kibana origin; the
bridge signs in through its own dedicated Chrome profile at profile_dir,
created by the bridge, never your everyday browser profile.
poll_timeout_s is how long one async search may run (1..600, default 120).
max_phrases caps distinct phrases per query, filters and aggregations together
(0..16, default 8; 0 turns text queries off).
vocabulary.fields: identifier fields whose every value is read from the cluster,
so a name in text with nothing marking it is labelled. The read happens ONCE per
cluster when the bridge signs in, back over vocabulary.days days ONE DAY AT A TIME,
newest first, one field and 1000 values per request (a page over the whole range was
measured at 31-297s against 8-35s over a day); each day is saved under out/es/ (0600)
as soon as it is whole, and the newest end is topped up every ten minutes.
Cases are refused with code vocabulary_building only until the last two days are in;
after that they run while the older days are still being read, and a name logged only
in a day not yet covered is not known yet - es-smoke's VOCAB line shows the covered
range. Every field is asked for its distinct count (one cheap request) before it is
paged, and a field with more than vocabulary.max distinct values is never paged: if
this section does not list fields, that field is LEFT OUT of the vocabulary and the
build carries on - its values then stay readable in message text, and es-smoke's VOCAB
line names it and its count as OVER CAP, NOT READ, which is the only place you are told;
if this section DOES list that field, the day is abandoned instead, naming the field.
The count is approximate, so a field within 5% of the cap is read whichever way lets the
build finish. ONE DAY taking longer than budget_s seconds (default 1200, twenty minutes;
it is per slice, so a slow day fails alone and is retried) also abandons that day and
leaves the saved vocabulary untouched. A site whose fields make one day cost more than
budget_s must raise it (ceiling 7200) or list fewer fields. Name fields only:
never user accounts, ids, addresses or numbers (refused at load). With no section at all the
default is every field that could be listed, which is what this list spells out;
listing fewer is allowed, and es-smoke's VOCAB line then names the fields left out,
whose values stay readable in message text.
Hits from a data stream name its backing index (.ds-<stream>-<date>-<gen>);
list the stream pattern (logs-app-*), never the .ds- names.
A malformed file is a startup error, never a silent skip.
